content:
The image shows soybean leaves with numerous angular, reddish-brown to dark brown spots. Some leaves exhibit yellowing around the spots, and there are signs of the spots merging into larger necrotic areas. Some leaf tissue appears to be falling out, giving a slightly ragged look. These features most closely match the description of Bacterial Blight, which mentions "angular lesions on leaves progressing from yellow-brown to dark reddish-brown centers with yellowish-green halos" and "infected tissue may fall out giving leaves a ragged appearance". While Brown Spot has similar initial symptoms (angular, red to brown spots), the presence of yellowish-green halos and the "ragged" appearance are more specific to Bacterial Blight.
